thread:
oliver: Quick brain dump: propose a 'burst pool' admission layer that sits between token budgets and concurrency limits. want thoughts before a formal RFC.

sana: Burst pool sounds useful for smoothing legitimate spikes. how does it interact with tenant weights?

oliver: Each tenant gets steady tokens + an optional burst allocation from a global reservoir. when reservoir is low we fall back to tokens. tenant weights influence fair share of the reservoir under contention.

peri: API shape? single RPC that returns both token and burst info or separate admit + reserve calls?

oliver: Minimal sync call to decide: admit or reject + optional burst_ttl. accounting async. example: POST /admit {client,route,est_tokens} => {allowed, burst_ms, tokens_reserved, abuse_score}. keep it tiny.

noah: Abuse score compute now or later? heuristics then ML?

oliver: Start with heuristics (failed completions, repeat short prompts, high retry loops, geographic anomaly). normalize 0..1 so policies can map score->penalty.

sana: Penalties: reduce burst_ms or flag for token multiplier?

oliver: Prefer shortening burst_ms first — simpler and avoids changing billing math.

peri: Streaming users could hold bursts forever. need renew or heartbeat semantics?

oliver: Yes, bursts are single-request. streaming re-admit per-chunk (e.g., every 4s or 2k tokens). make renew explicit in prototype.

noah: Implementation constraints: admit path <5ms and no sync DBs.

oliver: We'll use sharded in-memory reservoir + async persistence. no sync DB on fast path.

sana: Private/dedicated customers will want local control. make controller pluggable?

oliver: Contract = admit + accounting endpoints. driver swap supported so hosted controller or local policy engine can implement same interface.

peri: Fairness edgecases: micro-tenants might starve when many bursts happen.

oliver: We apply a pro-rata cap and reserve a small per-tenant floor so tiny customers keep some baseline. floor + reservoir weighting should prevent starvation.

noah: Rollout plan? feature flags and canaries?

oliver: Prototype sidecar wired to quota cache with burst disabled by default. FF to enable bursts for low-risk routes, then canary tenants, then wider rollout once metrics look good.

infra-bot: Sandbox deploy scheduled: burst-pool-proto v0.1 @ 2026-04-02T20:00Z :rocket:

sana: I'll add a small dashboard (lease_grant_rate, lease_expiry_rate, p99 latency, false_rejects) and a synthetic abuse harness.

noah: Audit logs: store minimal envelope for compliance (client, route, tokens, burst_ms, abuse_score).

oliver: Agreed. Sensitive payload excluded.

peri: Ok, this is a good precursor to an RFC. oliver, can you sketch the admit proto and a small simulation script?

oliver: Yes — i'll open a prototype PR with sidecar, admit shim, and a simulation that injects mixed-rate tenants. will tag you all. Thanks for quick feedback.
